name: Maii
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Maii (maii1238) is not in the catalog. The only title-keyword hit, Auer 1989 'Some ways to count morae', is a Glottolog false positive: Glottolog attached it to Maii [mmm] by automatic assignment from the word 'morae' (Maii alt. name Mae-Morae). I fetched sources the author's open FreiDok offprint, logged) and read the text: it is about German dialects (OHG, Bavarian, Alemannic) and Germanic/Latin/Greek mora counting, with no mention of Maii or any Oceanic language. Relevance: other-language-or-variety; priority none. No first-hand statement of Maii word stress was found in this sweep; Glottolog lists only Tryon 1976 (wordlist) and Tryon 1996 for the language, and the Wikipedia page carries no phonology.

earlier_scan.note: Vanuatu; Glottolog shows only Tryon 1996 subclassification comment and endangerment sources; no description found

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: a comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603. Canberra: ANU. Section 2.1.3 'Vowels and stress', p.16.
sources.note: Family-level only: 'Word stress in PNCV was most likely on the penultimate vowel. This is its position in almost all daughter languages for which phonological descriptions exist, where the historic final syllable is intact.' Maii is not a sample language; it appears only in two lexical entries (miu+vo=vo, -iul). No Maii-specific statement.

sources.citation: ABVD wordlist 'Maii' (id 1075), 187 items, source Tryon 1976; Greenhill, Blust & Gray 2008 database
sources.note: Wordlist only, no stress marking, no notes.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1996. Mae-Morae and the languages of Epi (Vanuatu). In John Lynch & Fa'afo Pat (eds), Oceanic studies: proceedings of the First International Conference on Oceanic Linguistics, 305-318. Pacific Linguistics C-133. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C133.305
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: No statement of stress placement. Paper is about stem-initial consonant alternation and realis/irrealis morphology. Only incidental remarks: p.312 (all Epi languages) 'once the vowel of the realis marker was lost (normal in unstressed position)'; p.317 (Maii mblakən) 'And /i/ would normally become /a/ in unstressed position'. Neither says where stress falls.

sources.citation: VanBib: a database of references to resources on Vanuatu languages, v1.3 (Zenodo 2025), rows for maii1238
sources.note: Lists for Maii only: Tryon 1976, Tryon 1986, Tryon 1996, Early 2004 (periphrasis), Crowley 1991 (OL 30), ABVD/ACD/ASJP wordlists, plus the Auer 1989 and Gronnum & Basboll 2001 'morae' false matches. No phonology of Maii exists in the bibliography.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for maii1238 (references: Tryon 1996; Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no descriptive reference beyond Tryon 1996 (verb morphology). Glottolog's 'Auer 1989' attachment is a computerized false match on 'morae'.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. Section 3.10.5 'Mkir' p.104; summary table 3.10.7 p.106.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.104: 'Tryon (1996a) is the only modern source for this language, which represents an account of the development of verb-initial mutation patterns, while Tryon (1976) includes some lexical information under the name Mae-Morae.' Table p.106, row Mkir: Phonology 'no', Grammar 'no', Lexicon 'brief', Other 'none'.
No phonology section, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Early, Robert. 1994. A grammar of Lewo, Vanuatu. PhD thesis, ANU. (Chapter 3.4 Stress = Lewo only; Maii/Mae-Morae mentioned pp.17, 30-31 and in morphology footnotes citing Tryon nd 'Notes on Mae-Morae' typescript)
sources.note: Stress section concerns Lewo only (penultimate-counting, weight-sensitive). Maii is mentioned only for speaker numbers, names (Mkir, Mari, Mgir), negation and realis morphology, with reference to an unpublished Tryon typescript 'Notes on Mae-Morae'. Nothing on Maii stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. 1986. Stem-initial consonant alternation in the languages of Epi, Vanuatu: a case of assimilation? In Geraghty, Carrington & Wurm (eds), FOCAL II, 239-258. Pacific Linguistics C-94. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement; p.253 repeats the diachronic remark that the realis-marker vowel was lost 'which would be normal in unstressed position'. Maii data are verb-stem alternation pairs only.

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU. vi+550 pp. (Mae-Morae = communalect 141 in the sound-correspondence tables, list 143 in the Appendix wordlists)
sources.note: Nothing for Maii. Ch. 2 gives only POC consonant/vowel reflex tables per communalect; p.40 (PDF p.46) row 141 Mae-Morae: a | a,ə(fn4 'Reflex unexplained') | ə | ə,Ø(fn6 'V2 is normally lost in di-syllables') | i,u | Ø. Footnote 7 'In unstressed syllables' belongs to row 130 Mapremo (Lewo), not Mae-Morae. Section 3.1.2 p.74: wordlists are 'a broad phonetic transcription', no phonemic analysis; the Mae-Morae wordlist carries no stress marks. No stress rule stated anywhere in the 552 pp.

sources.citation: PARADISEC, 'VEPI - Vanuatu - Epi Island and Adjacent Islands - Arthur Capell (1902-1986), Guide to Records' (Capell field notes: comparative wordlists incl. 'Mari (Maii)', Tasiko grammar note)
sources.note: Finding-aid only; lists wordlists and phrases for Epi languages including Mari (=Maii); no phonology or stress notes mentioned. The PARADISEC catalog itself (language_code=mmm) returned a Cloudflare challenge (403).

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. n.d. Notes on Mae-Morae. Unpublished typescript (cited in Early 1994, A grammar of Lewo, pp. 4320, 4419, 6695, 9617 of text; Tryon nd:2, nd:10).

sources.note: The only known grammatical sketch of Maii; Early cites it for articles, causative prefix, negation and realis marking. If any phonology/stress note on Maii exists, it is here. Whereabouts unknown (Tryon papers, ANU/PARADISEC?).

sources.citation: Budd, Peter. 2009. Topics in the grammar of Bierebo, Epi Island, Vanuatu. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London. c. 493 pp.

Repository (eprints.soas.ac.uk) was offline in earlier attempts.
